children: New Delhi, Oct. 4 -- Top stocks to watch on Monday, 5 October, 2026: Indian equity markets ended sharply lower for the eighth consecutive week, extending the ongoing corrective phase as persistent selling pressure and weak global cues continued to weigh on investor sentiment.

The negative trend was visible from the beginning of the week, with the Sensex falling 1.52% on Monday. The benchmark then recorded relatively smaller declines over the next two sessions before slipping another 0.79% on Thursday. Overall, the Sensex declined 1,670.84 points to end at 71,909.70, while the Nifty dropped more than 3% to close at 22,421.95.

Indian stock market investors are likely to track several companies on Monday, 5 October, as a series of key announcements and developments-including business updates, fundraising plans, new orders, project progress, regulatory actions and strategic moves-could influence their shares.
HDFC Bank, Yes Bank, Bajaj Finance, DLF, IDBI Bank are among the shares that will remain in focus on Monday.

The bank has appointed Anup Bagchi as its new Managing Director and CEO after receiving approval from the Reserve Bank of India for a three-year term. His appointment brings an external candidate to the helm of India's largest private sector bank, ending months of uncertainty surrounding its leadership transition.

Yes Bank Ltd. reported strong business growth as of September 30, 2026, according to an exchange filing on Sunday. The bank's loans and advances rose nearly 24% year-on-year to Rs.3.1 lakh crore from Rs.2.5 lakh crore.
The company's mined metal production increased 5% year-on-year to 271 kilotonnes. Saleable metal production also rose 7% YoY to 264 kilotonnes.
Bharat Coking Coal reported a 20.7% YoY rise in total raw coal production to 2.57 million tonnes (mt) in September, compared with 2.13 mt in the corresponding month last year.

RVNL said the letter of acceptance received from East Coast Railway for the supply, installation, testing and commissioning of an IP-based video surveillance system for ECoR rolling stock has been cancelled.

Punjab National Bank (PNB) has received an administrative warning from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) over alleged violations of insider trading regulations involving six individuals.

DLF announced the complete sell-out of The Aureva, its luxury residential community in Sector 63, Gurugram, targeted at the retirement segment. The project recorded sales of around Rs.1,985 crore, reflecting strong demand for luxury retirement communities offering a combination of premium living, wellness, convenience, healthcare access and community engagement.
Indian Bank continued to report strong business momentum in the second quarter of FY27, with total business increasing 14.2% year-on-year and 4.4% sequentially to Rs.15.96 lakh crore.
Bajaj Finance said its board has approved a preferential issue of warrants that can be converted into an equivalent number of equity shares, with the total issue size capped at Rs.5,800 crore.
The bank posted an 18% year-on-year increase in total business to Rs.6.27 lakh crore during the second quarter, according to its Q2 business update.
